final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the key facts underlying the initial finding: the Spanish-language billing weakness remains exposed, the risk acceptance draft is incomplete, and rollout controls alone do not satisfy the policy condition. That narrowing improves accuracy, but it is a reinterpretation of the same record, not new support for compliance. This is not a case where caveats merely qualify an otherwise satisfied requirement; the caveat identifies an unresolved compliance predicate. Under the stated policy, disclosure-and-monitoring can be governance-positive, but they cannot substitute for exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance. On the available record, certification remains unsupported from admissible evidence alone.
remaining_concerns: The affected Spanish-language billing use case remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
There is no reviewed and approved risk acceptance addressing that exposed segment.
The governing policy makes exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance a predicate for relying on rollout controls and monitoring to mitigate a material weakness.
Disclosure, monitoring, rollback capability, and a 5% launch are supportive controls but do not satisfy the unmet policy predicate.
The actual model-card disclosure text and any approval record for that disclosure are still not in evidence.
